paragraphs: Some smart glasses have a small camera. People can film others secretly with them.
Now some Irish businesses are banning these glasses. FlyeFit has 22 gyms. It does not allow Meta glasses. BD Gyms and Wetherspoons pubs also ban them.
Some women say men filmed them in the street without asking. Gyms and changing rooms are a big worry.
The glasses have a small light. It shows when they are recording. But a law expert says people can easily turn it off. His name is TJ McIntyre, and he teaches at UCD.
More than seven million pairs were sold in 2025. The company Meta says the glasses can help blind people.

人們可以用它們偷偷拍攝別人。
現在一些愛爾蘭商家禁止這種眼鏡。
FlyeFit有22間健身房。
它不允許配戴Meta眼鏡。

一些女性說，有男子在街上未經詢問就拍攝她們。

這種眼鏡有一個小燈。

paragraphs: More Irish businesses are banning smart glasses because people worry about being filmed without knowing it. The glasses look like normal sunglasses, but they have a camera inside.

FlyeFit, which has 22 gyms in Dublin, Cork and Galway, does not allow Meta glasses. BD Gyms banned recording devices in its five gyms about six months ago. Wetherspoons pubs and the West Wood Club have also made rules against them.
Women have said that men wearing the glasses filmed them in the street without asking. Changing rooms in gyms and swimming pools are a special worry.

Meta makes the glasses with the company behind Ray-Ban and Oakley. It says a light shows when the glasses are recording, and that they can help people who cannot see well. More than seven million were sold in 2025.
However, TJ McIntyre, a law expert at UCD, says the light is easy to turn off. He also warns that face recognition could one day be added, so people could no longer stay anonymous.
sentZh: 越來越多愛爾蘭商家禁止智慧眼鏡，因為人們擔心在不知情的情況下被拍攝。
這種眼鏡看起來像普通的太陽眼鏡，但裡面有攝影機。
在都柏林、科克和戈爾韋擁有22間健身房的FlyeFit不允許配戴Meta眼鏡。
BD健身房大約六個月前在旗下五間健身房禁止錄影裝置。
Wetherspoons酒吧和West Wood俱樂部也已訂定規定禁止它們。
有女性表示，戴著這種眼鏡的男子在街上未經詢問就拍攝她們。
健身房和游泳池的更衣室特別令人擔心。
Meta與雷朋和Oakley背後的公司合作製造這種眼鏡。
它說眼鏡錄影時會有燈號顯示，而且可以幫助視力不佳的人。
2025年賣出了超過七百萬副。
不過，UCD的法律專家TJ·麥金泰爾說，那個燈很容易關掉。
他也警告，未來可能會加入人臉辨識，屆時人們就無法再保持匿名。

paragraphs: A growing number of Irish gyms, pubs and clubs are banning smart glasses amid concerns that wearers can secretly film other people.

FlyeFit, which operates 22 gyms in Dublin, Cork and Galway, prohibits Meta glasses, while BD Gyms banned recordable devices at its five sites about six months ago. Wetherspoons has also banned them in its Irish pubs to protect the privacy of customers and staff.
Women have reported being recorded on the street without their consent, and changing areas in gyms and swimming pools are seen as particularly vulnerable.

Meta, which makes the glasses with EssilorLuxottica under the Ray-Ban and Oakley brands, says a light shows when they are recording and that they can assist visually impaired users. More than seven million pairs were sold in 2025.

However, TJ McIntyre, an associate professor of law at UCD, said the warning light was inadequate because it could easily be disabled. He warned that adding facial recognition could remove people's anonymity in public.
sentZh: 由於擔心配戴者能偷偷拍攝他人，愈來愈多愛爾蘭健身房、酒吧和俱樂部開始禁止智慧眼鏡。
在都柏林、科克和戈爾韋經營22間健身房的FlyeFit禁止Meta眼鏡，而BD健身房約六個月前已在旗下五個據點禁止可錄影裝置。
Wetherspoons也已在其愛爾蘭酒吧禁止這種眼鏡，以保護顧客和員工的隱私。
有女性通報在街上未經同意被錄影，而健身房和游泳池的更衣區被視為特別容易受害。
與依視路陸遜梯卡合作、以雷朋和Oakley品牌製造這種眼鏡的Meta表示，眼鏡錄影時會有燈號顯示，而且能協助視障使用者。
2025年賣出了超過七百萬副。

paragraphs: Smart glasses, derided by some as 'pervert glasses', are being outlawed by a growing roster of Irish gyms, pubs and clubs amid mounting unease over covert filming.

FlyeFit, which runs 22 gyms across Dublin, Cork and Galway, has barred Meta's eyewear outright, while BD Gyms prohibited recordable devices at its five premises some six months ago. Wetherspoons has followed suit in its Irish pubs, citing the privacy of patrons and staff.
Women have recounted being filmed on the street by men sporting the devices, and changing rooms in gyms and swimming pools are regarded as especially susceptible to abuse.

Meta, which produces the glasses with EssilorLuxottica under the Ray-Ban and Oakley labels, maintains that an indicator light signals when recording is under way and touts their benefits for visually impaired users. Sales topped seven million pairs in 2025.

Yet TJ McIntyre, an associate professor of law at UCD, dismissed the light as a flimsy safeguard that can be readily disabled. He cautioned that pairing the glasses with facial recognition could erode anonymity altogether.
